transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Morales (Redwood SE), Ravi Singh (Redwood CSM), Dr. Laura Chen (Apex Head of AI), Marcus Green (Apex Platform Eng), Isha Patel (Apex CTO)

[00:00] Samir: hi everyone thanks for joining, happy to do the qbr, uh we wanted to run through usage trends, cost, reliability, and the roadmap items, cool?
[00:18] Dr. Laura: yep thanks Samir, appreciate it. we got a couple folks here from infra because the latency spikes last month caused delayed triage alerts so we want to understand root cause and options.
[00:35] Marcus: yeah hi, Marcus here. typical week we see a clear morning spike 08:00 to 11:30 UTC and then again at 18:00 local. during those windows tail latency jumps to about 700ms per response.
[00:50] Jenna: ok noted, we pulled traces, looks like KV cache cold starts plus some batching fall-throughs when traffic is bursty, also a couple requests hitting a larger model variant by routing rules.
[01:10] Isha: just to add, cost is creeping up — token spend up 28% q/q and it's starting to impact our forecast. we want recommendations to stabilize both cost and latency.
[01:25] Samir: totally. quick agenda: 1) usage & cost deep-dive, 2) reliability + incidents, 3) roadmap options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), 4) recommendations and next steps. sound good?
[01:40] Dr. Laura: yep go ahead.

[02:05] Jenna: alright, on usage - over the last 90 days your top routes are: clinical-summarize (40% tokens), patient-chat (30%), and batch-index (20%). the clinical-summarize route uses a 70B open model with per-token cost higher than some smaller variants. also we see a lot of short requests under 64 tokens but many repeated prefixes which could benefit from prefix caching.
[02:35] Marcus: that matches our logs. question — is there an easy way to pin a lower-cost model for non-critical batches? we can't risk quality loss during summaries though.
[02:48] Samir: yes, you can set route-level model pinning and a canary rollout. recommended: keep clinical-summarize on the 70B for gold traffic, create a lower-cost 30B variant for non-clinical or draft runs and route 10-15% there for evaluation.
[03:10] Dr. Laura: okay can we automate fallback during capacity issues? last month we saw automatic fallbacks to an even smaller model but outputs were unacceptable.
[03:22] Jenna: the runtime supports automatic fallback but you control the policy. we can configure quality thresholds and automatic revert; also can configure structured confidence checks to divert low-confidence outputs for human review rather than full fallback.

[03:50] Marcus: on the latency spike, you mentioned KV cache cold starts — what's causing that? we persist KV cache on dedicated nodes right now?
[04:02] Jenna: correct, you're on hosted with some cached instances spun down between bursts. cold starts happen when cache miss + model warmup coincide with the burst. Dedicated or Private with pinned workers would greatly reduce that.
[04:20] Marcus: what's the expected latency improvement if we move to Dedicated reserved capacity?
[04:30] Samir: ballpark: 30-50% lower tail latency during peaks depending on provisioning. also more predictable 99th percentile. cost-wise Reserved Dedicated reduces per-token unit cost if commit utilization is high — but there is an up-front monthly commit.
[04:45] Isha: budget constraints — we can't justify large monthly commits yet. any mid-ground?
[04:52] Jenna: yes, two options: 1) Configure burst capacity — reserved baseline + on-demand burst; 2) Optimize batching/quantization on current hosted routes to cut cost by ~15-25%. we can run a cost-savings simulation using your traffic traces.

[05:15] Dr. Laura: can we see the simulation?
[05:18] Samir: we'll send it post-meeting. Jenna, we should include recommended quantization profile per route.
[05:23] Jenna: yea — for clinical-summarize recommend int8 quant with fp16 fallback on critical tokens; for patient-chat use 4-bit quant where acceptable. also adjust batching windows during low-latency critical windows so you don't increase P95.

[06:00] Marcus: on security/compliance — Apex is HITRUST-adjacent, we need assurances around data residency and KMS control if we move to Private.
[06:12] Samir: understood. Private offers customer-managed KMS and VPC peering, plus audit logs and SOC2 compliance. we can share the security pack (SOC2, ISO, encryption at-rest/in-transit) after this call.
[06:30] Isha: and how about onboarding for an on-prem/private deployment? timeline?
[06:36] Jenna: typical private deployment timeline is 6-10 weeks for VPC-managed cloud private; on-prem can be 10-16 weeks depending on infra. for Apex we'd start with a scoping call to map network and storage requirements.

[07:00] Dr. Laura: we also want guaranteed model version pinning. we've had drift in model weights when autosync happened on another vendor.
[07:10] Samir: you can pin model versions and disable auto-updates. rollouts are controlled by the config layer; there's also an audit trail for model loads.

[07:30] Marcus: any known gotchas with our current infra? we use k8s autoscaling and a rabbitMQ layer for job fanout. sometimes backpressure cascades.
[07:44] Jenna: rabbitMQ backpressure + request bursts can overwhelm a small pool; recommend smoothing at the ingress and enabling continuous batching settings in the runtime. that reduces amplification.

[08:05] Ravi (CSM): quick note — adoption metrics look healthy but growth is concentrated in 2 teams; recommend internal training to broaden usage and reduce peaks.
[08:18] Dr. Laura: yes we have two pilot teams. we'll add adoption goals in the next quarter.

[08:40] Samir: ok let's go through the incident in August — Marcus, can you summarize impact?
[08:47] Marcus: during a nightly deploy we had a scale-down and some caches were cleared; combined with a burst of batch-index jobs which used a large model, resulting in 40% degraded throughput for ~22 minutes.
[09:05] Jenna: we traced it to two things: aggressive autoscaler cooldown + routing rules that didn't prefer cached workers. we recommended adding sticky routing policies and longer cooldowns for your busiest routes.
[09:20] Isha: are these changes risky to apply? we prefer small incremental changes.
[09:26] Jenna: low risk — config-only changes. we can test on a canary route first.

[09:50] Dr. Laura: about cost — can you break down token spend by route and show opportunities?
[09:56] Samir: yes summary now: monthly token spend is $124k, clinical-summarize is $62k (50%), patient-chat $37k (30%), batch-index $18k (15%), misc 5%. potential optimizations: pin cheaper model variants for drafts, enable prefix caching, tune batching. estimated savings range 15-30% depending on aggressiveness.
[10:30] Marcus: that's helpful. what's effort to implement prefix caching?
[10:35] Jenna: engineering effort is small — config + a short profiling run, ~1-2 sprints to validate.

[10:50] Isha: about SLAs — what uptime SLA do we get on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[10:58] Samir: Hosted standard: 99.9% availability target; Dedicated: SLA-backed with 99.95% depending on commit tier; Private has an SLA option with enterprise contract. we'll include detailed SLA doc.

[11:20] Marcus: one more — do you support key rotation and HSM-backed KMS?
[11:25] Jenna: yes, private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations, and rotates keys per your policy.

[11:40] Dr. Laura: ok roadmap alignment — we're planning a rollout of priority triage feature in Q4 that will require lower latency and higher throughput. can Redwood support a pilot?
[11:52] Samir: absolutely. recommendation: pilot on Dedicated reserved baseline with smaller commit, plus burst, or start with a Private trial if you need KMS/VPC. for immediate wins, implement caching and batching optimizations to smooth latency.

[12:15] Marcus: what's the next concrete step to evaluate Dedicated without long commit?
[12:20] Samir: we can do a 30-day evaluation pool (trial capacity) and run benchmarks against your traces — low commitment. I'll scope costs in the report.
[12:34] Isha: perfect.

[12:50] Jenna: action items recap: we'll run the cost-savings sim, share recommended quantization/batching config, and produce latency traces. Samir will include financials and trial proposal. Marcus will share logs.

[13:10] Dr. Laura: timeline on those?
[13:14] Samir: we'll send the report and simulation by 2026-09-20; tech deep dive scheduled week of 2026-09-21; Jenna's config by 2026-09-22.

[13:30] Isha: ok that's good. any blockers from Redwood's side?
[13:34] Samir: none. we'll also attach the security pack for private deployment and SOC2 docs.

[13:50] Marcus: small note — please obfuscate any PII in logs we upload.
[13:54] Jenna: yes we'll confirm data handling procedures.

[14:10] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the report and next meeting invite.
[14:15] Dr. Laura: thanks all.

[14:48] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript had typical mis-hearings (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache"), some speaker attributions generic; cleaned minimally to preserve meeting fidelity.
